title: Etch-a-Sketch
body:
Goal: draw with the arrow keys, like the classic drawing toy.

  1. Open starter.py and press Run. Click the turtle window once, then press the Up arrow. Nothing happens!
  2. TODO 1 add screen.listen() so the window hears the keys. Run, click the window, press Up: the turtle draws a line.
  3. TODO 2 write go_down(), go_left() and go_right(), like go_up().
  4. TODO 3 connect the keys with screen.onkey(...). Careful: write screen.onkey(go_down, "Down") with no () after go_down.
  5. TODO 4 make c shake the drawing clean with pen.clear().
  6. Draw your nickname, a house or a maze!

Keys: arrows draw, space lifts or lowers the pen (the turtle turns into an arrow when the pen is up), n picks the next color, c clears.

Done looks like: every key does what the help text at the top says.

Extra: add w and s to make the pen thicker and thinner, or a key that writes your nickname at the turtle's position.

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Read the comments at the top of starter.py about handlers. The program sets up what each key should do, then waits. Right now the window is not paying attention to the keyboard yet.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: screen.listen() makes the window hear keys. screen.onkey(function, "Key") links a key to a function. New functions like go_down() work just like go_up() but use a different heading. pen.clear() wipes the drawing.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: Shape to fill in: screen.onkey(____, "Down"). Put the function name there with no (). A new function looks like def go_down():, then pen.setheading(____), then pen.forward(STEP). Put screen.listen() right before turtle.done().

starter.name: starter.py
starter.raw:
# Etch-a-Sketch
# Event-driven: the program sets up "handlers" (functions) and then WAITS.
# When a key is pressed, turtle calls the matching handler for us.
#   screen.onkey(go_up, "Up")   means "when Up is pressed, call go_up"
#   (no brackets after go_up: we hand over the function, we do not call it)
# Do the TODOs in order. Press Run, then CLICK the turtle window once so it
# can hear your keys.

import turtle

STEP = 10
COLORS = ["#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#009E73", "#CC79A7", "#000000"]
HELP = "Arrows: draw   space: pen up/down   n: next color   c: shake clean"

settings = {"color": 0}   # which color from the list we are using


def go_up():
    pen.setheading(90)
    pen.forward(STEP)


# TODO 2: write go_down(), go_left() and go_right() like go_up().
#         Headings: down = 270, left = 180, right = 0.


def pen_up_or_down():
    """Space bar: lift the pen if it is down, put it down if it is up."""
    if pen.isdown():
        pen.penup()
        pen.shape("arrow")    # the shape shows the pen is up (not color alone)
    else:
        pen.pendown()
        pen.shape("turtle")


def next_color():
    """n: move to the next color in the list (back to the first after the last)."""
    settings["color"] = (settings["color"] + 1) % len(COLORS)
    pen.pencolor(COLORS[settings["color"]])


def shake_clean():
    """c: like shaking a real Etch-a-Sketch - the drawing disappears."""
    # TODO 4: clear the pen's drawing with pen.clear()
    pass


if __name__ == "__main__":
    screen = turtle.Screen()
    screen.title("Etch-a-Sketch")

    helper = turtle.Turtle()
    helper.hideturtle()
    helper.penup()
    helper.goto(0, 260)
    helper.write(HELP, align="center", font=("Arial", 14, "normal"))

    pen = turtle.Turtle()
    pen.shape("turtle")
    pen.pensize(3)
    pen.speed(0)
    pen.pencolor(COLORS[0])

    screen.onkey(go_up, "Up")
    # TODO 3: connect "Down", "Left" and "Right" to your new functions,
    #         and connect "space", "n" and "c" to the functions above.

    # TODO 1: the window is not listening for keys yet! Add:
    #         screen.listen()
    turtle.done()          # wait for events until the window is closed
